newsitem.title: LEBANON: Beirut court slaps jail terms in forged money case.
newsitem.headline: Beirut court slaps jail terms in forged money case.

text.p: A Beirut court on Thursday sentenced to jail six people, including an Eritrean envoy and a wealthy Lebanese businessman, for smuggling forged dollars to Turkey and Africa.

The court sentenced in absentia Hadeesh Malo, former Beirut envoy of the Eritrean Liberation Front, and two accomplices to eight years jail while Beirut businessman Ghassan Matraji and two others in custody were given five years imprisonment.
Malo was convicted of smuggling $1 million in forged dollars in a suitcase to African states in 1989, when he represented the Eritrean revolutionary faction in Lebanon and held a diplomatic passport.

Matraji was convicted of providing the counterfeit money which he obtained in Lebanon's eastern Bekaa Valley, a hotbed for the drugs and counterfeit money trade during the lawlessness of the 1975-90 civil war.
He also provided forged dollars smuggled to Turkey in 1990 by one of the other accomplices.
In March 1996, Matraji was sentenced to nine months jail by a Beirut military court for smuggling arms to and from Lebanon and arming sectarian militias during the 1975-90 civil war.
He is also standing trial on charges of leading a gang that smuggled drugs to Holland and Canada. Sentencing in that case is expected next month.
